summary: Open-source platform to trace, evaluate and monitor LLM apps and AI agents, self-hosted or on Comet's cloud.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Opik, built by Comet, records what your LLM app or AI agent does so you can debug and improve it. It traces LLM calls, tool calls and multi-step agent runs as trace trees, evaluates outputs with datasets, experiments and LLM-as-a-judge metrics (for example hallucination detection), manages prompts with a playground, and monitors production with dashboards and online evaluation rules. It has Python and TypeScript SDKs, OpenTelemetry support and many framework integrations. The full platform, including the backend, is open source.
sixtySeconds.problem: LLM apps fail in ways that are hard to see. Opik shows every step and gives you tests and metrics to catch problems before and after release.
whoFor: AI teams moving from prototype to production
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it for a fully open-source, self-hostable tracing and evaluation platform that isn't tied to one framework.
requirements: Docker for self-hosting the server, or a free Comet account for the cloud

overview: Install the SDK with pip install opik and run opik configure to point it at Comet's cloud or your own server.
Add the @track decorator to a function and every call, including nested calls, is logged as a trace.
To self-host, clone the repo and run ./opik.sh (or opik.ps1 on Windows), then open localhost:5173. Apache-2.0 licensed.
